newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Cocoa seen sideways despite recent rise.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Cocoa seen sideways despite recent rise.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE cocoa futures were still seen trading sideways despite recent gains.

July cocoa was called to open about five to six stg lower despite two consecutive positive closes this week. Some traders called the market slightly lower because of the lack of follow-through buying in New York on Tuesday.

CSCE July cocoa closed up $5 at $1,435 per tonne, but that was only in the middle of the day's range. It traded between $1,442 and $1,425 on Tuesday to fill a chart gap between $1,432 and $1,441 before paring gains again.

Some traders had bought at London's close on Tuesday in anticipation of a further rise by New York's close. But New York's lacklustre finish was likely to dampen sentiment at London's start on Wednesday, traders said.
Adrian Haylor, technical analyst at Sucden, also said London cocoa futures were likely to open lower due to sterling's rise overnight above $1.64 and 2.80 against the mark.
Despite an expected weaker opening, traders said cocoa would likely remain rangebound without any clear technical or fundamental signs to push the commodity's price in either direction.
"It's a range-trading market," Haylor said. He said September looked comfortable for now trading between key support at 1,000 and resistance between 1,033 and 1,035.
Haylor pegged strong September resistance near the top of its recent range at 1,050.

He said September cocoa's moving averages were going sideways, hovering just above the market near 1,033 and 1,034. He also said relative strength indices (RSIs) have neutralised from slightly oversold territory last week.
